ideas.title: Agencies can run security audit sweeps on cheap models after a pass-every-run qualifier
ideas.connection: The audit skill packages agent-run security review, and the video shows only one of four cheap Chinese flash models fixed security holes in every run.

ideas.title: Aggressive local quants need repetition-loop tests before they touch document pipelines
ideas.connection: Unsloth's 1-bit quant claims 91% top-1 retention, but that check does not measure repetition loops, and Boo Bench's 179 loop-triggering pages plus llama.cpp's fixed reasoning budget make a cheap, predictable loop test for local runs.

ideas.title: Security audit findings can open ServiceNow tickets owned by the engineer who ran them
ideas.connection: The Cloudflare audit skill produces machine-readable findings, and AgentCore Gateway now lets an agent call ServiceNow as the calling user with no custom token code.

ideas.title: Shared agent skill files become a serving cost lever, not just a style guide
ideas.connection: HiCache turns repeated prompt prefixes into cache hits across parallel serving, and mattpocock/skills shows teams converging on shared skill files that every agent session loads first.

ideas.title: Training teams can ship every policy deck in many languages with one approved voice
ideas.connection: On 2026-11-01 Magpie suggested training teams rebuild narrated, on-brand decks on one workstation whenever a policy changes; VoiceStudio adds fully local voice cloning and dubbing, so the same rebuild can produce every language version in one approved narrator's voice.

builds_on.title: Training teams can regenerate narrated, on-brand decks locally whenever a policy changes

ideas.title: Inference buyers should rerun hardware bake-offs now, because kernels swing cost per token
ideas.connection: AMD's 2x per-dollar claim depends on AITER tuning, vLLM v0.33.0 final ships a gfx950 AITER fix, and agent-written Hopper kernels add up to 38% decode speed, so software now moves the hardware ranking.

ideas.title: Back offices can serve self-checking OCR at scale and route doubtful pages
ideas.connection: vLLM 0.33.0 adds MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 and Nemotron Parse 3.5, giving production serving to an OCR model that assesses its own correctness.

ideas.title: Platform teams can gate every agent skill install behind a scan this quarter
ideas.connection: The Cursor Marketplace backdoor shows agent add-ons are a live supply chain risk, npx skills gives one install path to control, and SkillSpector can scan skills for injection and exfiltration before that path lets them through.

ideas.title: Teams shipping HTML previews can have a repo agent file sandbox-hole issues
ideas.connection: The ChatGPT exploit gives a concrete pattern to hunt for, the Cloudflare skill is a widely adopted agent-run security audit, and DeepSeek's proactive agent works a repo through issues and PRs without waiting for a prompt.

ideas.title: Self-hosted Git servers become the hidden bottleneck for persistent agent teams
ideas.connection: OpenRig wires Claude Code, Codex and Pi into persistent teams with owned work, and OpenAI's Pando account shows agent development volume forced a rebuild of a Git backend.

ideas.title: Due diligence code audits can run live with the target's engineers present
ideas.connection: On 2026-10-23 Magpie suggested due diligence consultants could security-audit an acquisition target's code on one laptop with Flint on Rapid-MLX, a Graphify code map and an audit skill; today's Rapid-MLX 0.16.9 reuses prompt state so a repeated ~32K-token prompt starts in 0.39 s instead of 18.6 s, turning each follow-up question from a wait into a conversation.

ideas.title: Security audit findings can open ServiceNow tickets owned by the engineer who ran them
ideas.connection: The Cloudflare audit skill produces machine-readable findings, and AgentCore Gateway now lets an agent call ServiceNow as the calling user with no custom token code.

ideas.title: Due diligence consultants can security-audit an acquisition target's code entirely on one laptop
ideas.connection: Flint runs fast on a Mac via Rapid-MLX, Graphify gives it an auditable map of the codebase, and Cloudflare's audit skill turns that into verified, machine-readable findings, all without code leaving the machine.

ideas.title: Teams can prototype on cheap MiniMax API then self-host the identical model
ideas.connection: M3.1 Flash was available as a cheap 1M-context API, and now its open weights serve on SGLang, so a product can move in-house without changing models.

ideas.title: Shared agent skill files become a serving cost lever, not just a style guide

ideas.title: Enterprises can shift Claude workloads to whichever cloud has unspent committed budget
ideas.connection: Claude is now generally available under Google Cloud IAM and billing while already offered on Bedrock with structured outputs, so the same workload can be billed against either cloud commit.

ideas.title: Defense and government contractors can run code agents on air-gapped laptops with inspectable context
ideas.connection: Flint provides a laptop-class open coding model, Graphify gives it local repo context with explained edges, and OpenCode supplies the open agent loop, so the whole stack runs with no network calls.
